result.description:
Community Worker

Business: CoreAssist Pty Ltd
Location: Yagoona NSW 2199
Employment Type: Full-time, Ongoing
Salary: AUD $75,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation

Full Job Description

About the Business
CoreAssist Pty Ltd is a registered NDIS provider based in Yagoona, New South Wales, delivering personalised disability support services to participants across Sydney, Western Sydney, and surrounding communities. The organisation provides a broad range of services including Supported Independent Living (SIL), daily living assistance, support coordination, community participation, life skills development, mental health support, aged care, transport assistance, household tasks, home modifications, and specialised disability support programs. 
CoreAssist is committed to empowering people living with disabilities to achieve greater independence, social inclusion, and improved quality of life through person-centred, culturally responsive, and outcome-focused support services. The organisation works collaboratively with participants, families, carers, allied health professionals, support coordinators, and community organisations to deliver tailored support solutions aligned with individual goals and NDIS plans. CoreAssist operates under strong values of compassion, integrity, inclusiveness, accountability, innovation, and respect while maintaining full compliance with NDIS Practice Standards and relevant Australian legislation. 
As demand for disability and community support services continues to increase, CoreAssist requires an experienced Community Worker to coordinate participant supports, facilitate community engagement, promote independence, and ensure participants receive high-quality, person-centred services that enable them to achieve their personal goals.

About the Role
The Community Worker is responsible for assessing participant needs, developing and implementing individual support strategies, coordinating access to community resources, monitoring participant progress, and assisting individuals living with disabilities to maximise independence and community participation.
Working closely with participants, families, allied health professionals, support coordinators, healthcare providers, and external agencies, the Community Worker plays an important role in delivering holistic support that promotes inclusion, wellbeing, personal development, and positive participant outcomes consistent with CoreAssist's person-centred service model. 
The position requires excellent communication, interpersonal, organisational, and problem-solving skills together with a genuine commitment to improving the lives of people living with disabilities.

Key Responsibilities
•	Conduct participant interviews and comprehensive needs assessments to identify individual goals, strengths, risks, and support requirements.
•	Develop, implement, monitor, and regularly review individual support plans consistent with participant goals and NDIS plans.
•	Support participants to develop independent living skills, social skills, confidence, and community participation.
•	Assist participants to access healthcare, allied health, housing, education, employment, transport, recreational, and other community support services.
•	Facilitate participant involvement in community activities, life skills programs, recreational programs, and social inclusion initiatives.
•	Monitor participant wellbeing, evaluate service outcomes, maintain accurate case notes, and prepare progress reports.
•	Provide advocacy, information, guidance, and practical assistance to participants and their families regarding available community services and supports.
•	Liaise with support coordinators, allied health professionals, healthcare providers, government agencies, carers, and community organisations to coordinate integrated service delivery.
•	Identify barriers affecting participant independence and implement appropriate support strategies to promote positive outcomes.
•	Maintain confidential participant records, service documentation, incident reports, and case management records in accordance with NDIS Practice Standards and organisational policies.
•	Promote participant rights, dignity, choice, privacy, cultural inclusion, and person-centred practice at all times.
•	Participate in multidisciplinary meetings, quality improvement initiatives, and ongoing professional development.
•	Assist CoreAssist in maintaining compliance with NDIS Practice Standards, Work Health and Safety legislation, Child Safe requirements, and organisational policies.
•	Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance participant satisfaction, service quality, and organisational performance.


Requirements
•	Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
•	AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Community Services, Disability, Human Services, Welfare, Individual Support, or a closely related field, or at least three years of relevant experience may substitute for formal qualifications where applicable (ANZSCO Skill Level 2).
•	Demonstrated experience working within disability services, community services, aged care, or NDIS-funded programs.
•	Strong understanding of person-centred practice, participant rights, safeguarding principles, and community service delivery.
•	Sound knowledge of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), disability support services, community resources, and participant-centred care.
•	Excellent communication, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills.
•	Strong organisational, problem-solving, and case coordination abilities.
•	Ability to maintain accurate participant records and prepare professional reports.
•	Compassionate, empathetic, reliable, and participant-focused approach to service delivery.
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
•	Current NDIS Worker Screening Check, National Police Check, Working with Children Check (where applicable), and Current First Aid/CPR certification or willingness to obtain.
•	Current Australian Driver Licence is desirable.

Work Conditions
•	Full-time, ongoing position.
•	Standard operational hours with flexibility based on participant needs and service delivery requirements.
•	Work is performed across participant homes, community settings, CoreAssist facilities, and outreach locations throughout Sydney.
•	Ongoing professional development and training opportunities.
•	Collaborative and supportive multidisciplinary environment committed to empowering participants and promoting independence.
•	Opportunity to contribute to meaningful community outcomes through high-quality, person-centred disability support services.

Solicitor 
Gun Law Office – Knoxfield, VIC, 3180 
Permanent, full-time | $80,000 – $85,000 plus superannuation 

About us

Gun Law Office is a legal practice located in Knoxfield, Victoria, providing legal services to individuals, families and businesses.

The firm advises and represents clients across a range of practice areas, including commercial law, corporate law, business transactions, commercial and retail leasing, property law, wills and estates, trusts, family law, family violence matters, civil litigation and general legal advisory work.

The practice assists clients with both transactional and dispute-related matters, including legal advice, document preparation, negotiations, court and tribunal processes, settlements, powers of attorney, affidavits, statutory declarations and cross-border legal documentation.

Due to the evolving needs of the practice, Gun Law Office is seeking a suitably qualified Solicitor to join its team on a permanent, full-time basis.

The role 

We are seeking a qualified Solicitor to assist with the day-to-day conduct of client matters, from initial instructions through to finalisation, under the supervision and direction of the Principal and senior legal practitioners where required.

The role will involve assessing client instructions, identifying relevant legal issues, conducting legal research, preparing advice and correspondence, drafting and reviewing legal documents, managing client files, and assisting with negotiations, settlements, court processes and tribunal matters.

The successful candidate will be expected to work across both advisory and dispute-related matters, including preparing matters for conferences, mediations, hearings and other procedural events. The role also involves regular liaison with clients, counsel, courts, tribunals, government authorities, settlement agents, other legal practitioners and external stakeholders.

This position requires strong legal drafting, research, analytical and communication skills. The successful candidate must be able to manage competing deadlines, maintain accurate file records, exercise sound professional judgement and ensure all work is performed in accordance with professional, ethical and regulatory obligations.

 Key duties and responsibilities 

•	Take client instructions, identify legal issues and assist in advising clients on appropriate legal options and processes.
•	Conduct legal research and prepare advice, correspondence, file notes, case summaries and other legal documents.
•	Draft, review and settle affidavits, statutory declarations, court documents, contracts, leases, settlement documents, powers of attorney, wills and other legal instruments.
•	Assist with commercial, corporate, property, conveyancing, leasing, wills and estates, trusts, family law, family violence, civil litigation and dispute resolution matters.
•	Prepare matters for court, tribunal, mediation and conference attendances, including reviewing evidence, preparing chronologies, briefing counsel and arranging supporting documents.
•	Attend and appear before courts and tribunals where appropriate, including the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia, the Magistrates’ Court of Victoria, VCAT and other relevant courts and tribunals.
•	Assist with negotiations, settlements and dispute resolution processes in accordance with client instructions and under supervision.
•	Liaise with clients, counsel, courts, tribunals, government authorities, settlement agents, other legal practitioners and external stakeholders.
•	Manage client files under supervision from commencement to completion, including maintaining accurate file records, diarising deadlines and monitoring matter progress.
•	Prepare, review and witness powers of attorney, statutory declarations, affidavits, certifications and other Australian or overseas legal documents requiring execution, attestation or authentication.
•	Assist with cross-border legal documentation, including powers of attorney, statutory declarations, affidavits and related documents used in Sri Lankan or other overseas legal matters.
•	Ensure all work is performed in accordance with professional conduct rules, ethical obligations, confidentiality requirements, court rules, regulatory obligations and firm procedures.

Required qualifications, experience and skills 

•	Admission as an Australian legal practitioner; 
•	Current Victorian practising certificate, or eligibility to hold one; 
•	Bachelor of Laws, Juris Doctor or equivalent qualification; 
•	At least one year of relevant legal experience in private practice, in-house practice, litigation support, family law, property law, conveyancing, commercial advisory work or related legal work; 
•	Strong legal drafting, research, communication and file management skills; 
•	Ability to prepare and review legal correspondence, court documents, affidavits, contracts, leases, settlement documents, wills, powers of attorney and other legal instruments; 
•	Ability to manage competing deadlines, work under supervision and attend courts, tribunals, mediations, settlements and client conferences as required; and 
•	Professional proficiency in Sinhala will be highly regarded as many of the firm’s clients require language support to provide accurate instructions and properly understand legal advice and documents.

How to apply 

We welcome applications from all appropriately qualified candidates. Gun Law Office is committed to a fair and inclusive recruitment process and will consider applicants based on their qualifications, skills, experience and suitability for the role.

Your application should include:

•	A current resume outlining your qualifications, admission status, practising certificate status and relevant work experience; and
•	A one page cover letter addressing your suitability for the role.

To ensure all applications are properly received and assessed, please submit your application via one platform only and do not apply through multiple job portals.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Implement SoftwareDefined Networking (SDN) and develop programmatic, APIdriven workflows across network hardware using automation tools such as PowerShell, Bash, Python, and RESTful integrations to improve operational efficiency and system reliability. 

Monitor and analyse network traffic, capacity, and utilisation metrics, and evaluate endtoend network infrastructure performance across all corporate office locations. 

Evaluate and propose technical enhancements to network operations, interconnected server infrastructure, internal hardware, distributed PropTech applications, and hybrid operational environments. 

Optimise 4K media-rendering architectures and secure localised Network attached Storage (NAS) configurations, improving internal high-volume data-pipeline workflows for the marketing division. 

Oversee network and system configurations to ensure smooth data flows between real estate-specific APIs, external listing syndications (e.g., Realestate.com.au, Domain), and internal master CRMs. 

Provision, test, and deploy complex server networks, cloud systems (Microsoft 365, Azure Active Directory / Entra ID), and endpoint systems using modern Mobile Device Management (MDM) software. 

Formulate comprehensive testing strategies to validate network throughput, failover systems, and server redundancy, ensuring the agency maintains its strict zero-downtime metric during business hours. 

Provide expert troubleshooting and fault-finding services to isolate, diagnose, and resolve intricate network bugs, hardware failures, system anomalies, or cross-platform software conflicts. 

Troubleshoot complex issues across hardware, networks, software, database applications, servers, and workstations, coordinating with internal teams and vendors, and maintaining high service standards. 

Actively contribute to ZED Real Estate’s Information Security Management System (ISMS) by supporting the implementation and upkeep of its policies, procedures and controls, ensuring the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information in alignment with ISO/IEC?27001. 

Design and execute network security baselines, including Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW), Zero-Trust conditional access rules, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and advanced endpoint detection systems. 

Architect and manage Identity and Access Management (IAM) lifecycle workflows to enforce continuous security baselines across automated user onboarding and offboarding frameworks. 

Create, test, and preserve robust data backup structures, comprehensive disaster recovery workflows, and Business Continuity Plans (BCP) to secure sensitive real estate escrow accounts and high-net-worth data.

A Bachelor’s degree or higher qualification in Network Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a closely related ICT Major. 

At least 5 years of relevant professional experience as a Network Engineer, Systems Engineer, or ICT Systems Administrator in a corporate setting 

Professional infrastructure certifications are highly regarded (e.g., Cisco CCNA/CCNP, Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator, CompTIA Security+). 

At least 5 years demonstrated experience of core networking models and protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, BGP, VPN, switching, routing). 

At least 5 years experience managing corporate directory platforms and infrastructure identities (Microsoft cloud technologies, including Microsoft 365, Entra and Intune). 

Must have over 5 years’ experience to implement, administer, and troubleshoot network infrastructure devices, including wireless access points, firewall, routers, switches, controllers 

Must know how to setup virtual configurations in VMWare vSphere and Hyper-V 

At least 5 years of experience with server virtualisation, cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), and hybrid integration projects. 

Strong analytical skills and sound administration skills 

Quick to grasp new ideas and concepts 

Ability to work to tight deadlines and under immense pressure at times
